sections.text:
The holy month of Ramadan approached, and Juha could not stand fasting and felt extremely hungry and thirsty, so he was impatiently counting the remaining days until the end of the month.

In order not to forget the number of days he fasted, Juha devised a very simple method of counting.

Juha brought an empty pottery jar and placed it in the corner of his room. He decided to put a small pebble in it every day after breakfast, so that when thirty pebbles were filled in it, Eid would have come.

Ramadan began, and on the first day, Juha placed a pebble, and on the second day, he placed a second pebble, and he followed this system precisely.

But his young and naughty son was watching his father with curiosity, and one day, when Juha went out to pray, the son crept into the room carrying a large handful of pebbles that he had collected from the garden.

The naughty son threw all the pebbles in his hand into his father's jar to fill it quickly, then ran away!
Several days later, Juha was sitting in a café with his friends, and one of them asked him: “Oh Juha, you are a careful and wise man. How many days have passed since Ramadan until now?”

Juha said confidently: “Wait for me a moment, I will go to my house to see my exact number and tell you the correct number!”

Juha returned home, went to his room, and grabbed the jar to count the pebbles inside.

Juha was shocked to find the jar completely filled with pebbles! In fact, some pebbles were falling out of it due to the large amount of it!
Juha emptied the pebbles on the ground and began counting them in amazement: “Ten.

Twenty.

forty.

hundred.

One hundred and twenty pebbles!”

Juha could not believe his eyes. How could Ramadan this year be one hundred and twenty days long?!
Juha returned to the café, wiping the sweat from his forehead, with signs of shock and confusion evident on his face.

His friends asked him eagerly: “Hey Juha, how many days of Ramadan have passed?”

Juha replied in a low and hesitant voice: “My friends.

I don't want to frighten you, but based on my very precise calculations, exactly one hundred and twenty days have passed from the month of Ramadan until today!

The friends burst into laughter and sarcasm and said: “Are you crazy, Juha? The whole month has a maximum of thirty days, so how can one hundred and twenty days pass while we are still in the middle of it?!”

Juha responded to them very seriously while defending himself: “Believe me, I tried to be lenient with you and reduce the number as much as possible! If I told you the real number in the jar, Ramadan this year would continue for the next five years without interruption!”

Everyone laughed at Juha's naivety and his strange method of calculations, and Juha later realized that his son was the one who had tampered with the jar, so he stopped using this method and relied on seeing the crescent like other people.
